title: Landing page brief
description: Brief a landing page for one audience and one offer: the promise, the proof, the call to action, how visitors find it and how it is measured.

inputs.label: Audience segment and the problem it searches for, described without personal data
Product, feature or plan the page offers
Channels that will send visitors and the search queries targeted
Conversion goal and its current baseline

tool_actions.description: Publishing the page on the website or in a landing page builder.
Connecting the page's form to the CRM or marketing automation tool.

sections.title: Promise and audience
sections.prompt: Who the page is for and the outcome it promises, in the words that audience uses.

sections.title: Proof
sections.prompt: Customer results, figures or quotes, each with the evidence behind it.

sections.title: Why this rather than an alternative
sections.prompt: How the offer compares with the competitors and substitutes the visitor knows, from the market dossier.

sections.title: Call to action and form
sections.prompt: The single action asked of the visitor, each form field and why the follow-up needs it.

sections.title: Search and metadata
sections.prompt: Target query, page title, meta description and the internal links that lead to the page.

sections.title: Measurement
sections.prompt: Conversion event, tagged links, and the target compared with the baseline.

checks.verification: Each claim points to evidence the team can show: a measurement, a customer result or a dated source.
The form collects only what the follow-up needs and links to the privacy notice.
Keyboard navigation, contrast and form labels were checked against the WCAG 2.2 AA criteria the team applies.
A test conversion was recorded through a tagged link before launch.
